title: RL-PTQ: RL-based Mixed Precision Quantization for Hybrid Vision Transformers
problem: Existing quantization approaches incur significant accuracy loss when compressing hybrid convolution and transformer models with low bit-width. Determining optimal bit-widths and observers for mixed-precision quantization tailored to hybrid vision transformers is non-trivial.
motivation: Efficient inference of vision transformers through effective quantization enables deployment on memory-constrained and specialized hardware like PIM accelerators.
method: RL-PTQ compresses neural networks after training by automatically choosing bit-widths (how many bits to represent numbers in each layer) and observer configurations (how to measure each layer's behavior) using reinforcement learning—a machine learning technique where software learns by trying different choices and keeping the ones that work better. The method groups similar layers together in hybrid models (those that mix convolutional and transformer components) and trains an RL agent to discover the optimal quantization settings for each group. This targeted approach handles the unique challenges of mixed architectures better than simpler quantization methods that use the same settings everywhere.
key_novelty: Using reinforcement learning to automatically find optimal bit-widths and observer configurations tailored to each layer group in hybrid models that combine convolution and transformers.
contributions: RL-based post-training quantization framework for automatic mixed-precision configuration discovery
Achieves highest quantized accuracy for MobileViTs compared to previous PTQ methods
Demonstrates 10.1× energy efficiency on PIM accelerators and 22.6× on GPU versus baseline
Addresses quantization challenges specific to hybrid convolution-transformer architectures
